description: Generated contacts labeled with a known limit (labels, the generators' LIMITS), generated scenarios on some profiles (scenarios), and recorded sessions (sessions) that no signal a page can see gets right (palm README, Known limits). They are replayed and counted in the report but excluded from the gates. The list may only shrink: knownLimitsMax in thresholds.json caps the sessions plus scenario and profile pairs.

labels.slides-like-a-stroke: A palm part that slides 10 mm or more as it lands (further than a palm settles) and is smaller than a palm, or on a digitizer without sizes: a stroke or a scroll by every signal until a pen or a neighbour tells.
labels.bounce: A palm part down for under 300 ms, smaller than a palm or on a digitizer without sizes, that moves less than a palm settles: a dot or a quick short mark by every signal.
labels.fingertip-sized: A palm part that grows no larger than a fingertip (11 mm): a finger by its size, so alone it draws or scrolls like one.
labels.held-after-pen: A tap of the other hand within a second of the pen lifting: E8 holds it where the hand may be, anywhere while the side of the hand is unknown [S16].
labels.side-unknown: A pen that reports neither lean nor contact size, with no palm resting while it wrote: the hand may lie on either side, or above the line for a hooked or overwriting grip, so a touch there is refused.

scenarios.why: The pen reports no tilt, so the side of the writing hand, and its height for a hooked or overwriting grip, is known only once palms have rested while it wrote: until then the mirror image of the hand region counts as the hand. With no contact size either, a palm that re-plants on the unknown side and slides scrolls until the pen comes down.

The pen reports no tilt, so the side of the writing hand, and its height for a hooked or overwriting grip, is known only once palms have rested while it wrote: until then the mirror image of the hand region counts as the hand. With no contact size either, a palm that settles twice above the line, 20 s after the pen, is a two-finger double tap by every signal.

The pen reports no tilt, so the side of the writing hand, and its height for a hooked or overwriting grip, is known only once palms have rested while it wrote: until then the mirror image of the hand region counts as the hand. A 10 mm hand edge that bounces above the next line for a hooked or overwriting grip is a tap by its size and place.

The pen reports no tilt, so the side of the writing hand, and its height for a hooked or overwriting grip, is known only once palms have rested while it wrote: until then the mirror image of the hand region counts as the hand. A pinch of the other hand in the mirror image of the hand region, while the pen hovers, waits for the pen to leave.

The pen reports no tilt, so the side of the writing hand, and its height for a hooked or overwriting grip, is known only once palms have rested while it wrote: until then the mirror image of the hand region counts as the hand. A scroll of the other hand there within a second of the pen lifting is held like a palm bounce (E8). A pen that reports as a mouse never leaves range, so for 2 s after it stops the pen is near and a scroll needs far-side evidence.

The pen reports no tilt, so the side of the writing hand, and its height for a hooked or overwriting grip, is known only once palms have rested while it wrote: until then the mirror image of the hand region counts as the hand. With no contact size either, a double tap of the other hand there is refused, since a palm settling twice looks the same.

The pen reports no tilt, so the side of the writing hand, and its height for a hooked or overwriting grip, is known only once palms have rested while it wrote: until then the mirror image of the hand region counts as the hand. A tap on a control there while the pen hovers, or as a palm lifts and the region re-learns onto it, is refused.

A page tap of the other hand within 20 s of the pen, inside the hand region learned from resting palms (it grows to an 80 mm radius around the heel), waits for the pen to be away 20 s: a palm bouncing there looks the same.

The scenario places its resting hand as on a tablet: on a 64 mm phone screen the hand lies over the writing line and the screen edge, where a single-radius digitizer cannot tell a knuckle from the tip.
A single-radius digitizer rounds sizes in 4 mm steps, so on a phone a palm that slides as it lands reads as a 20 mm thumb stroke until it grows a step.

A palm that lands first and drifts under 10 mm beside where the tip will land: on one constant size, a phone screen, or with a palm part of thumb size, its drift may show or hold the draw slot until the tip lands beside it.
A palm that lands at fingertip size and grows: without contact sizes, or rounded to 4 mm steps on a phone, its growth is unseen and it draws like the tip until the tip lands beside it.
A single-radius digitizer hides a palm's growth inside a 4 mm step: a palm that lands at fingertip size may show its drift before it grows into the next step and is retracted.

A resting hand split in two parts, one of fingertip size, beside the writing tip: the small part may show, or pair with the tip as a pinch, before its size or the hand region tells; without sizes only its place does.
